questions.prompt: Which Navy player is nearest the net-front area?
questions.explanation: F1 is at net front, close to Gold’s crease.

questions.prompt: Choose two checks before treating a screened shot as useful.

options.text: Where F1 and the goalie are relative to the shot
Whether the puck can pass Gold 1
Whether net-front traffic guarantees a goal

questions.explanation: A screen is only part of the read; traffic does not establish a clear or successful shot.

options.text: Choose a shot or another available option

questions.explanation: Reading the shooting-lane defender and checking the net-front picture can overlap or happen in either order; this is one workable pattern, not the only scored timeline. Choosing to shoot or use another option still comes last, since the release depends on what those reads show.

questions.prompt: Move YOU toward a different point-to-slot shooting angle.
questions.explanation: Moving toward the middle changes the line around Gold 1. Recheck traffic instead of assuming the old screen still applies.

questions.prompt: F1 moves away before release. Which two checks are useful now?

options.text: Recheck the shot lane and available passing options
Check whether any useful screen remains
Shoot immediately even if the lane has changed

questions.explanation: The screen was a changing cue, not a permanent property of the shot.

questions.prompt: Why should feedback avoid saying that a screened point shot is always best?
questions.explanation: A blocked lane, changed traffic or a better pass can alter the decision. The picture cannot prove scoring probability.

questions.prompt: What should YOU communicate before the point shot?

options.text: F1 is near the net-front lane; check the screen and support
A screened goalie view is enough to decide the release

questions.explanation: The message names the screen relationship while leaving shot value conditional.

questions.prompt: Which two cues affect a screened shot?

options.text: Whether F1 remains a useful screen
Whether F2 or the slot lane is reachable

questions.explanation: Screen quality and support affect the choice; the label does not prove a useful attempt.

questions.prompt: Move YOU to a different point-to-slot angle with F1 visible.
questions.explanation: This changes the shooting line while retaining the screen relationship.

questions.prompt: F1 moves away before release. What changes in your explanation?
questions.explanation: The screen cue is gone, so compare a new shot lane with a pass or protected touch. The original plan needs a fresh read.

reasons.issue: Sequence question implied a mandatory look-decide-execute order (read lane defender, then check net-front picture, then choose) for two reads that can genuinely overlap or occur in either order, contradicting AUTHORING-CONTRACT.md's explicit rule against forcing an artificial scan order.
reasons.change: Replaced the explanation with wording that states the first two reads can overlap or happen in either order (this is one workable pattern, not the only scored timeline) while explaining that the shoot/other-option choice still comes last because it depends on those reads. Options, answer key and every other question/field are unchanged verbatim.
reasons.evidence: AUTHORING-CONTRACT.md, Answer and teaching contracts: "Sequence belongs only where order itself teaches something useful... Do not imply a player must stop scanning, wait to look for pressure, or follow an artificial 'look, decide, execute' order for every read." Precedent: calibration-adjudication.md U13-010 q3, resolved the same way (clarify overlap in the explanation rather than remove the sequence format).

sourceChecks.scope: Fetched and read the PDF directly (pages 18-19, the "Shooting" slides). Confirms bullet content: "Watch for goalie looking around a screen and shoot appropriately," "Get shots through...miss their F. Be able to slide and shoot. This directly supports the scenario's screen/traffic-read teaching objective and the specific F1-in-shooting-lane framing. It does not certify these exact coordinates, ages, or a guaranteed shot outcome.
